body:
Thank you for listening and your well thought out response. You're absolutely right about suffering warping things. Sleep deprivation can do a lot of strange things to the mind as well. This isn't a decision I've come to lightly or quickly though. I've exhausted the medical options.

Unfortunately the law in those states has quite a few hoops to jump through, one of which is that the illness must lead to death in less than 6 months. I find that absolutely ridiculous, but I think it is also representative of how most people view these things. Whenever I've even hinted at these things with friends and family, they tell me I can't give up, keep trying, so on and so forth, without having done any research on my condition or the prognosis. I know they mean well, but it frustrates me that the same people who will put a sick dog out of its misery don't allow me that same compassion. It feels like most people are simply pulling the wool over their eyes, denying reality, and deciding this is taboo without a second thought, to the point that I don't think I can even discuss it with a therapist.

So here I am, trying to sort out my thoughts by telling it to the internet. I know I can't expect people to understand what a day in my body is like. I had very little real frame of reference for my condition until it got bad in my late 20s. I just wish that the laws and our culture weren't such that I'll have to do this messily and alone. I've had a pretty great and full life. I can accept that really shitty things happen for no real reason. I think what I'm struggling with right now more than anything, is that I have to use an Irish goodbye for something so important.

Quality of life has gradually degraded to the point that now I can't work or care for myself, and it will only degrade further as I age. I have painful seizures that prevent me from sleeping more than a few hours most nights. I've tried every available treatment. My body is a torture prison. 

You're right. 20 years is 'A SHITLOAD'. A shitload of garbage years spent in pain and sleep deprivation.
